newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 10.00 cents higher.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 10.00 cents higher.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 10.00 cents per lb higher on Monday, as traders expected the market to bounce back after Friday's massive sell-off, traders said.
Some traders said London's inability to reach its $500 lower opening due on Monday also contributed to the higher call.
London robusta futures tumbled 12 percent early Monday in a speculative-led sell-off. LIFFE July was down $300 at the midday break, to $2,170, and September also dropped $300, to $2,200.

Friday, New York arabica futures plummeted as speculators rushed to take profits following a explosive three-day rally to 20-year highs. July tumbled 38.40 cents per lb, to 276.40 cents, after ranging between 311.00 and 273.00. September plunged 35.50 cents, to 238.30 cents, while the back months dropped 23.15 to 28.40.
The July/September spread, a barometer of near-term supplies, narrowed to 38.10 cents from 41.00 cents at the close on Thursday. September/December shrank to 37.90 cents from 45.00 cents on Thursday.
Technically, traders said July would run into some resistance at 288-290 cents.
On the fundamental side, Weather Services Corp. said Monday no damaging cold is expected this week in Brazil's coffee belt. Temperatures will near to above normal, they said.
